The image shows a cross-section of a corn stalk broken at a node with:
- Very dark/black outer rind at the node
- White to tan pith inside
- Node snapped/broken cleanly
- No pink/red coloration

This points strongly to **Physoderma_stalk_rot** (black node, snapping) or possibly **Anthracnose_stalk_rot** or **Diplodia_stalk_rot**. Let me check reference images.

The Physoderma_stalk_rot reference (bottom-left panel) shows a stalk broken at the node with a dark/black outer ring and white pith — very similar to the test image. Let me check a couple more candidates.

The evidence is clear:

- **Test image**: Cross-section of a corn stalk broken at a node, with a very dark/black outer ring at the node and white/tan pith inside.
- **Physoderma_stalk_rot reference** (bottom-left): Nearly identical — stalk broken at the node, black node ring, white pith center. Description: "Plants break at the first or second node, which appear black with possible pith rot; infected nodes snap easily when gently pushed."
- **Charcoal_stalk_rot**: Shows shredded pith with vascular strands — not matching.
- **Anthracnose_stalk_rot**: Shows shiny black blotches along the outer rind, shredded internal structure — not matching.
- **Diplodia_stalk_rot**: Shows brown/tan dry rot with pycnidia near nodes — not matching.
- **Bacterial_stalk_rot**: Shows soft/slimy collapse — not matching.

The black node with snapping/breaking is the hallmark of Physoderma stalk rot.
